source_row.rationale: CDC describes pain out of proportion to local skin findings, rapid progression, systemic toxicity, bullae or necrosis as warning features of necrotizing fasciitis. It is a surgical emergency; imaging can assist in selected cases but should never delay surgical exploration when clinical suspicion is high.
source_row.source_detail: Current CDC guidance: pain out of proportion, rapid progression and systemic findings heighten suspicion; imaging should never delay surgical exploration; prompt surgical management is essential.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Clinical Guidance for Type II Necrotizing Fasciitis
source_row.stem: A client with a soft-tissue infection develops rapidly progressive swelling, severe pain out of proportion to visible skin findings, high fever, and hypotension. What is the priority interpretation?
